jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 10/16/2026 Maintenance Support Member - St. Marks National Wildlife RefugeSummaryAmerican Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), is seeking one member to contribute to maintenance projects under the mentorship of St Marks National Wildlife Refuge (NWR) Staff.For more information about ACE, please visit our website.Start Date: 11/02/2026 (Flexible start date available)Estimated End Date: 1/23/2027 (or 12 weeks later after the anticipated start date)*a 12 week minimum commitment is required, approximately 480 hours.Location Details/Description: St. Marks National Wildlife Refuge; St. Marks, FLThe Refuge was established in 1931 to provide wintering habitat for migratory birds. It is one of the oldest refuges in the National Wildlife Refuge System. It encompasses over 83,000+ acres spread out between Wakulla, Jefferson, and Taylor counties, and includes about 43 miles along the Gulf Coast of northwest Florida. The Refuge includes coastal marshes, islands, tidal creeks and estuaries of seven north Florida rivers, and is home to a diverse community of plant and animal life. The Refuge also has strong ties to a rich cultural past, and is home to the St. Marks Lighthouse, which was built in 1842 (current tower) and is still in use today.For more information about North Florida Refuges Complex, please visit the FWS website.Position Overview: The mission of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) is working with others to conserve, protect, and enhance fish, wildlife, plants, and their habitats for the continuing benefit of the American people. The member will also do facilities maintenance including, but not limited to, general upkeep, cleaning, small repairs and administrative documentation.This individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promotes exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. PLC projects also include specific eligibility requirements such as age and citizenship. Please contact ACE staff with questions about eligibility, or view general eligibility information on our website.Housing: ACE members may be accommodated in provided FWS housing at no cost for the duration of the term, depending on availability. Compensation for this position begins at $29.00 per hour.Role Summary: Quantum Signal AI is looking for a Real-Time Software Intern to help develop performant, low-level, and embedded software during the summer of 2027. Interns will gain new skills working on projects that span a variety of applications involving sensor integration, real-time networking, and infotainment hardware. microcontrollers, networking, custom electronics, and in-vehicle hardware Collaborate with your mentor alongside other software, electrical, mechanical, and research engineers as part of multidisciplinary project teams Develop tests and execute test plans Create and collaborate with others on supporting documentation What You’ll Bring: Active enrollment in a Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related degree program, with student status maintained through the academic term immediately following the internship Interest in low-level software, embedded systems, and hardware-facing development Understanding of when you need to ask for help/feedback and willingness to do so Experience gained through coursework, internships, club, personal projects, or other hands-on software development activities Strong programming fundamentals, including data structures, algorithms, and debugging techniques Experience troubleshooting software/hardware and systematically identifying root causes Experience developing software in C/C++ Experience working in Linux environments Bonus Points For: Familiarity with C/C++ development tooling (gcc, CMake, gdb, etc.) Familiarity with embedded, distributed, or multithreaded software Previous hobby, school, club, or work experience with: Microcontrollers (Arduino, STM32, ESP32, etc.) Real-Time Operating Systems (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, NuttX, etc.) Embedded or Real-Time Linux (Raspberry Pi, BeagleBone, etc.) Low-level serial protocols (I2C, SPI, UART, etc.) High-speed connectivity protocols (Ethernet, USB, CAN, etc.) Sensor processing and integration Video and/or audio processing and compression You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you are excited about this role and think you can bring value to Quantum Signal AI, we encourage you to apply! What You’ll Get: Frequent collaboration with a diverse set of teams at QSAI A rare level of work variety and hands-on experience A relaxed, fun community and environment in which to solve interesting problems Opportunity to participate in a 401(k) savings plan Ford A/X Plan vehicle discounts Mentorship-focused learning that emphasizes engineering fundamentals, hands-on problem solving, and understanding the underlying principles behind the systems we build. About QSAI: Founded in 1999, Quantum Signal grew up developing intelligent algorithms and AI. As our engineering R&D services expanded, we later sharpened our focus on applications and technology related to mobility, sensing, perception, autonomy, and simulation. In 2019 we became Quantum Signal AI, a subsidiary of Ford Motor developing technologies to advance their R&D efforts. We build solutions to enhance the capability, robustness, safety, and acceptance of intelligent ground vehicles in an effort to make transportation more effective and efficient for all. While AI is part of our name, our internship program emphasizes building fundamental engineering knowledge, analytical thinking, and practical problem-solving skills. We want interns to understand how and why systems work through hands-on experience, mentorship, and experimentation, rather than simply relying on tools to provide answers. Our HQ in the historic Union School in Saline, MI is the perfect playground to develop this cutting-edge technology and we’re always looking for smart folks who like new challenges, learning new skills, and technical variety.

information management, and maintenance of accurate and traceable records.Quality assurance and regulatory laboratory practices: Exposure to NHANES and CLIA-related activities will provide an understanding of quality systems, documentation protocols, standard operating procedures, data integrity protection, and the necessity of generating reliable laboratory results.Scientific data interpretation and problem-solving skills: You will learn to critically assess analytical runs, identify potential issues, analyze quality-control results, and make informed decisions regarding data applicable to roles in public health laboratories, clinical laboratories, academia, and the biotechnology/pharmaceutical industries.Mentor(s): The mentor for this opportunity is Zia Fazili-Qari (zxq0@cdc.gov). This infrastructure includes equipment such as electric motors, compressors, hydraulic systems, refrigeration systems, heaters, dryers, power systems, measurement and data acquisition systems, control systems, and more. We do not design or conduct analysis of the vehicles; we design, operate, and maintain the systems which enable ground test of models and subassemblies to provide our customers with the data they need to make decisions on design and flightworthiness. Open external candidates who are currently enrolled in an accredited college or university engineering or technical degree program noted in the qualifications. Job SummaryThe Beyond New Horizons internship program offers a 12-week full-time summer opportunity for undergraduate and graduate students pursuing degrees in various engineering and computer science related disciplines. As part of the internship, you are paired with experienced engineers and scientists who serve as your mentor(s) in completing real engineering or technical work gaining valuable experience in your field of study while contributing to Air Force and contractor missions. You will be required to present a briefing to management demonstrating what you learned and accomplished throughout the summer. Our internship is structured such that you are assigned multiple tasks to complete throughout the summer to provide exposure to the variety of types of work assignments available here at AEDC. These are real engineering/technical assignments that need to be completed, not busy work to keep you occupied. Test Operations Engineers also provide system engineer capabilities as part of a team of mechanical and electrical engineers whose job is to oversee installation, operation, sustainment, and troubleshooting of their assigned test cell equipment and systems. Some examples of test systems in various facilities include thrust determination and force measurement systems, fuel systems, icing systems, combustors, nozzles, water systems, gaseous nitrogen systems, hydraulic systems, lubrication oil systems, high pressure air systems, service air systems, liquid nitrogen systems, various sensors, etc. that are needed to reliably provide test data to our customers. This competitive and collaborative program attracts thousands of applicants each year. Simulating a real-world startup accelerator environment, the interns are divided into teams, each working on a different challenge project. Throughout the Games, interns receive mentorship from senior leaders, solve problems using Booz Allen’s products and unique engagement models, and leverage the power of collaboration in a team environment. The summer culminates with a final Challenge Cup competition and presentation to senior leadership. A past winner took the challenge of helping blind individuals navigate by using new technology and developing a business and market penetration plan. Teams have also helped to develop an app that gives military commanders an easy way to track real-time and open-source information about developing situations, including sudden attacks, fighting human trafficking, and even tracking the spread of a disease worldwide. Join us. The world can't wait. You Have: Experience in cybersecurity, including in an academic environment Knowledge of networking concepts, including the OSI model Knowledge of virtualization Knowledge of Linux and Windows systems Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in a Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field by Summer 2028 or Summer 2029 Nice If You Have: Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Possession of excellent critical thinking and analytical skillsPossession of excellent verbal and written communication skills Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. CompensationAt Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $53,000.00 to $108,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. jobs.description: Employer: Complete Omics Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Job Description:Compensation: Negotiable internship compensation based on qualifications, experience, and time commitment.Complete Omics Inc. is a venture-backed, commercial-stage biotechnology company located in the Baltimore, Maryland area. We develop and commercialize advanced omics-based platforms and solutions for precision medicine, health monitoring, and disease diagnostics.Complete Omics has two immediate openings for CLIA Laboratory Operations & Bioinformatics Interns. jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineering Intern at Gecko Robotics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Gecko Robotics, Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Role at a GlanceGecko Robotics is seeking a Full Stack Software Engineering Intern to join our Engineering team in New York for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.Gecko’s Engineering teams build customer-facing applications that turn robot, sensor, and document data into decisions about the health of critical infrastructure. You will work across the stack on a defined project: building frontend workflows, backend services, and data pipelines that make complex asset data usable by the people who maintain it. You will ship real features into a product that customers already rely on, with clear direction from a mentor and the room to own your piece of it.Due to government program requirements, candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.What you will doOwn a scoped full-stack project from design through deployment under the guidance of experienced engineers.Build user-facing features in React and TypeScript that support real operational workflows.Develop backend APIs and services in Python that ingest, transform, and serve structured and unstructured data.Design data models and schemas, and write the logic that parses, associates, and validates data from multiple sources.Use version control, code review, testing, and structured debugging to produce maintainable code.Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and Forward Deployment Engineers to understand how customers use the product, with the option to travel to a customer site during the summer.Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship.Technologies We UseReact, TypeScript, Python, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Git, Linux, and cloud infrastructure (GCP). Depending on the project, you may also work with LLM APIs and data-processing pipelines, 3D visualization, or containerized deployments. The specific tools will depend on the assigned project.About YouYou are a builder who likes seeing your work used. You are comfortable moving between frontend and backend, you break large problems into shippable pieces, and you communicate clearly about what you built, what you learned, and what you would do next.Required SkillsCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.Ability to work onsite in New York, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.Foundational programming experience in Python and JavaScript or TypeScript, including object-oriented or functional programming concepts.Experience building a web application end to end (frontend and backend) through coursework, projects, research, hackathons, or a prior internship.Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.Understanding of relational databases and REST APIs.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work, explain tradeoffs, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback.Preferred SkillsExperience with React and TypeScript in a real project.Experience designing data schemas or working with messy, real-world datasets.Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP, and to containers such as Docker.Exposure to integrating LLM or other AI APIs into an application.Interest in 3D, visualization, or spatial data.Interest in industrial, defense, or infrastructure applications where reliability matters.

jobs.title: Dams & Hydraulics Intern at GFT
jobs.description: Employer: GFT Expires: 10/17/2026 Program Timeframe: Mid-May through mid-August Join GFT, an award-winning architecture, engineering, and construction firm, as a Dams & Hydraulics Engineering Intern and gain real-world experience in a dynamic environment. Our inclusive environment will fuel your innovation and imagination while fostering a sense of belonging. Joining the Dams & Hydraulics team at GFT means helping protect communities and critical infrastructure through the design, evaluation, and rehabilitation of dams, levees, spillways, and other hydraulic structures. Our engineers work on some of the nation's most important water infrastructure projects, applying innovative solutions to improve dam safety, enhance resilience, manage flood risks, and extend the service life of aging facilities. Our multidisciplinary team brings together expertise in civil, structural, geotechnical, mechanical, and hydraulic engineering to solve complex challenges for dam owners across the country. From condition assessments and rehabilitation design to hydrologic and hydraulic analysis and risk-informed decision making, every project offers an opportunity to make a lasting impact. What you’ll be challenged to do:During your internship, you will work alongside experienced engineers on real-world dam and hydraulic structure projects. You'll receive mentorship and hands-on experience while contributing to meaningful engineering work that supports public safety and infrastructure resilience. You’ll collaborate with professionals across multiple disciplines, including structural, geotechnical, construction, mechanical, and hydrology and hydraulics. The majority of our interns convert to full-time employees. jobs.title: Postdoctoral Researcher at Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education
jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 10/17/2026 A post-doctoral research opportunity is available through the Department of Operational Sciences at the Air Force Institute of Technology.What will I be doing?As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will join a community of scientists and researchers studying adversarial interactions, multi-agent systems, and decision-making under uncertainty relevant to security and defense settings. Research activities will focus on methodological innovation, theoretical development, and applied mathematical/statistical modeling.Why should I apply?Under the guidance of a mentor, you will gain hands-on experience to complement your education and support your academic and professional goals. Along the way, you may engage in activities and research in several areas. These include, but are not limited to:Adversarial location and network interdiction modelsAdversarial machine learning attacks and defense (e.g., against Bayesian inference)Algorithmic development for bilevel (or multilevel) optimizationMethodological developments in Bayesian statistics and/or decision analysisApplication of adversarial risk analysis within security settingsWhere will I be located? Dayton, OhioWhat is the anticipated start date?Exact start dates will be determined at the time of selection and in coordination with the selected candidate. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis and fellowships will be filled as qualified candidates are identified.What is the appointment length? This appointment is a twelve-month research appointment, with the possibility to be renewed for additional research periods. Appointments may be extended depending on funding availability, project assignment, program rules, and availability of the participant.What are the provisions? You will receive a stipend to be determined by AFIT. Stipends are typically based on a participant’s academic standing, discipline, experience, and research facility location. Other provisions may include the following:Health Insurance Supplement (Participants are eligible to purchase health insurance through ORISE)Relocation AllowanceTraining and Travel AllowanceAbout AFITThe Air Force Institute of Technology, or AFIT, located at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the Air Force’s graduate school of engineering and management as well as its institution for technical professional continuing education. A component of Air University and Air Education and Training Command, AFIT is committed to providing defense-focused graduate and professional continuing education and research to sustain the technological supremacy of America’s air, space and cyber forces.About ORISEThis program, administered by Oak Ridge Associated Universities (ORAU) through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and DoD. Participants do not enter an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DoD or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE. For more information, visit the ORISE Research Participation Program at the U.S. Department of Defense.Qualifications The qualified candidate should hold or be currently pursuing a doctoral degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Statistics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a closely related field. A postgraduate is required to have earned their degree within 5 years of the appointment start date.A PhD is not required at the time of selection. Ideally, a participant will complete their PhD prior to the opportunity's start date; however, an "all but dissertation" status may be acceptable as well, provided the requisite research qualifications.Preferred Skills:Background in quantitative research, evidenced by peer-reviewed publications, academic presentations, or preprint manuscriptsKnowledge of Bayesian statistics, mathematical optimization, game-theoretic analysis, network problems, decision analysis, or behavioral economicsProficiency in a scientific computing or statistical programming languages (e.g., Python, R, Julia, C++, or MATLAB)Familiarity with mathematical programming solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX) or probabilistic/Bayesian computing frameworks (e.g., Stan, PyMC)Ability to formulate high-impact, novel and well-defined research questions from unstructured requirementsApplication RequirementsA complete application consists of:Zintellect ProfileEducational and Employment HistoryEssay Questions (goals, experiences, and skills relevant to the opportunity)Resume (PDF)Transcripts/Academic Records - Please upload a copy of a transcript for your current or most recent degree program that meets the disciplinary qualifications of the opportunity. Click here for detailed information about acceptable transcripts.One Recommendation. We encourage you to contact your recommender(s) as soon as you start your application to ensure they are able to complete the recommendation form and to let them know to expect a message from Zintellect. Recommenders will be asked to rate your scientific capabilities, personal characteristics, and describe how they know you. You can always log back in to your Zintellect account and check the status of your application.If you have questions, send an email to AIRFORCE@orise.orau.gov. Please list the reference code of this opportunity [AFIT-2026-0022] in the subject line of the email. Please understand that ORISE does not review applications or select applicants; selections are made by the sponsoring agency identified on this opportunity. All application materials should be submitted via the “Apply” button at the bottom of this opportunity listing. Please do not send application materials to the email address above.Connect with ORISE...on the GO! Download the new ORISE GO mobile app in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to help you stay engaged, connected, and informed during your ORISE experience and beyond!Stipend $6,500.00 – $8,250.00 MonthlyPoint of Contact LeslieEligibility Requirements Citizenship: LPR or U.S. CitizenDegree: Doctoral Degree received within the last 60 months or currently pursuing.Discipline(s):Computer, Information, and Data Sciences (2 )Engineering (2 )Mathematics and Statistics (5 )Other Non-Science & Engineering (1 )Social and Behavioral Sciences (2 )

Throughout the internship experience, you will receive direct feedback from peers and managers, engage with other interns in the program, and will have multiple learning opportunities through Lunch and Learn presentations and training courses. Our Intern Program is inclusive to all our US sites and is designed to give each intern a concentrated view of what it is like to be an engineer at Sensata.Internship projects vary from year to year and are based on current business needs at the time of the internship. jobs.feedName: Andrew J. Anagnost College of Engineering and Computer Science
jobs.title: AI/ Machine Learning Engineering Intern at Gecko Robotics, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Gecko Robotics, Inc. Expires: 10/17/2026 Gecko Robotics is seeking an AI/ML Engineering Intern to join our Engineering team in New York for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday.Gecko collects some of the richest inspection data in the world: ultrasonic and other non-destructive testing (NDT) measurements from wall-climbing robots, paired with the documents, drawings, and operational records that describe the assets they inspect. You will work on a defined project that turns that data into decisions, building models and the systems around them that run reliably on real customer data. This is an engineering internship, not an analytics one. We build the systems that analyze the data, not just the analysis.Due to government program requirements, candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.What you will doOwn a scoped machine learning project from problem framing through evaluation and integration, under the guidance of experienced engineers.Build data pipelines in Python that clean, label, and structure NDT sensor data, documents, or operational records for model training and inference.Train, evaluate, and iterate on models, and design evaluations that reflect how the output will be used in the field.Integrate a model or LLM-based workflow into a service or tool that other engineers and Forward Deployment Engineers can use.Investigate failure modes on messy, real-world data, document what you find, and recommend what to fix next.Use version control, code review, testing, and experiment tracking to produce work others can reproduce and build on.Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship.Technologies We UsePython, PyTorch or similar ML frameworks, NumPy and pandas, SQL, LLM APIs and agent frameworks, Git, Linux, and cloud infrastructure (GCP). Depending on the project, you may also work with signal-processing tools for ultrasonic data, document-processing and information-extraction pipelines, or orchestration tools such as Airflow. The specific tools will depend on the assigned project. About YouYou are an engineer who happens to work in machine learning. You care whether a model works on real data, not just on a benchmark, and you are comfortable owning the code around the model: the pipeline, the evaluation, and the integration. You approach new problems methodically, communicate clearly about results and uncertainty, and are excited to be the first person to look at a problem. Required SkillsCurrently pursuing a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028.Ability to work onsite in New York, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship.Strong programming experience in Python, including writing well-structured, tested code beyond notebooks.Coursework or project experience in machine learning, including training and evaluating models on real datasets.Working understanding of linear algebra, probability, and statistics.Working familiarity with Git or similar version control systems.Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain results, quantify uncertainty, and collaborate on ambiguous problems.Ability to independently close knowledge gaps, stay organized, and learn from feedback. Preferred SkillsGraduate-level coursework or research in machine learning, signal processing, or computer vision.Experience taking a model beyond a notebook: building a pipeline, an API, or a tool around it.Experience with LLM APIs, retrieval, information extraction, or document understanding.Experience with time-series or sensor data, especially ultrasonic, acoustic, or other physical measurements.Exposure to cloud infrastructure, preferably GCP, and to containers such as Docker.Interest in industrial, defense, or infrastructure applications where reliability matters.

jobs.description: Employer: Booz Allen Hamilton Inc Expires: 10/17/2026 University - 2027 Summer Games Systems Engineer Intern - El Segundo, CAThe Opportunity:The Summer Games is an innovative internship program that attracts some of the nation’s best and brightest students. The goal is to develop a breakthrough idea or solution for one of our customer's most pressing, complex, and multidimensional problems while developing valuable technical skills. This competitive and collaborative program attracts thousands of applicants each year. Simulating a real-world startup accelerator environment, the interns are divided into teams, each working on a different challenge project. Throughout the Games, interns receive mentorship from senior leaders, solve problems using Booz Allen’s products and unique engagement models, and leverage the power of collaboration in a team environment. The summer culminates with a final Challenge Cup competition and presentation to senior leadership. A past winner took the challenge of helping blind individuals navigate by using new technology and developing a business and market penetration plan. Teams have also helped to develop an app that gives military commanders an easy way to track real-time and open-source information about developing situations, including sudden attacks, fighting human trafficking, and even tracking the spread of a disease worldwide. Join us. The world can't wait. You Have:Experience with programming languages, including .NET, C++, JavaScript, Java, or Python in a professional, academic, or internship work environment Knowledge of software development best practices Ability to learn new languages and frameworks Ability to work in groups Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor’s degree in a Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics field by Summer 2028 or Summer 2029 Nice If You Have: Ability to produce technical documentation and create design artifacts Possession of excellent critical thinking and analytical skills Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills Clearance:Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. CompensationAt Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page. Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $53,000.00 to $108,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud. Candidate AI Usage PolicyAI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided. Work ModelOur people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration, whether it occurs in person or virtually. All interns will receive a meaningful project and an unparalleled experience. We’ll provide the tools and resources you need to learn. The challenging and creative work you do throughout your internship will directly impact the team you are contributing to. All internships will be conducted in-person. Hosting managers will determine when and how often interns work in the office. All interns will have the option to opt into relocation services (flights, trains, or car mileage reimbursement). Additionally, all interns will be provided with a living stipend to subsidize housing, utility, commuting, and miscellaneous costs. Program Requirements Currently enrolled in an associate’s, bachelor’s, or master’s degree program and graduating December 2027 – June 2028 Available to participate in a 12-week internship starting in mid-May or mid-June Currently residing in the US or open to relocating oneself to the US Exhibits learning agility; has the ability to think differently, and/or grasp and apply new skills and concepts Approaches problems in a clear, well-organized, and solutions-oriented manner Works well with others and contributes to team tasks Able to effectively communicate problems, solutions, needs, or priorities Is engaged, seeks to learn, and is able to manage time effectively A passion for significantly impacting game development Applicants must apply with a resume and codes samples to be considered Internship Opportunities Rendering Intern:Work on console, PC, and mobile titles to solve problems within render architecture, systems programming, GPU microcode, procedural geometry, ray tracing, and performance analysis and optimization. Requirements:Working knowledge of C++ Experience with at least one game-related domain (graphics, networking, embedded systems) Multi-threading, optimization (rendering and systems), and computer architecture are a plus Practical facility in an additional language like Python or Rust Hosting Locations: Central Technology (Portland, ME & Sherman Oaks, CA) Graphics Engineering Intern:This intern will be contributing to the graphical code base, delivering graphical features, pipeline support, and tools development to improve the visual fidelity of our games. Requirements:Working knowledge of C++. Experience working with HLSL Experience working with Vulkan or DirectX 12 Strong knowledge of 3D Math/Linear Algebra Hosting Locations: Central Technology (Portland, ME) & Treyarch (Playa Vista, CA) Our World At Activision, we strive to create the most iconic brands in gaming and entertainment. We’re driven by our mission to deliver unrivaled gaming experiences for the world to enjoy, together. We are home to some of the most beloved entertainment franchises including Call of Duty®, Crash Bandicoot™, Tony Hawk’s™ Pro Skater™, and Guitar Hero®. As a leading worldwide developer, publisher and distributor of interactive entertainment and products, our “press start” is simple: delight hundreds of millions of players around the world with innovative, fun, thrilling, and engaging entertainment experiences. We’re not just looking back at our decades-long legacy; we’re forging ahead to keep advancing gameplay with some of the most popular titles and sophisticated technology in the world. We have bold ambitions to create the most inclusive company as we know our success comes from the passionate, creative, and diverse teams within our organization. We’re in the business of delivering fun and unforgettable entertainment for our player community to enjoy. And our future opportunities have never been greater — this could be your opportunity to level up. Ready to Activate Your Future? The videogame industry and therefore our business is fast-paced and will continue to evolve. As such, the duties and responsibilities of this role may be changed as directed by the Company at any time to promote and support our business and relationships with industry partners. We love hearing from anyone who is enthusiastic about changing the games industry. Not sure you meet all qualifications? Let us decide! Research shows that women and members of other under-represented groups tend to not apply to jobs when they think they may not meet every qualification, when, in fact, they often do! At Activision Blizzard, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment and strongly encourage you to apply. Activision Blizzard is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, protected veteran status, or any other basis protected by applicable law and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. We are committed to working with and providing reasonable assistance to individuals with physical and mental disabilities. If you are a disabled individual requiring an accommodation to apply for an open position, please email your request to accommodationrequests@activisionblizzard.com General employment questions cannot be accepted or processed here. Thank you for your interest.

jobs.title: Embedded Systems & FPGA Research Intern at OpalAI
jobs.description: Employer: OpalAI Expires: 10/17/2026 OpalAI — NASA SBIR Project: Runtime Health Monitoring for Aerospace SystemsInternship Duration: 3–6 monthsPosition Type: Internship / Research & DevelopmentLocation: Los Angeles, CA / Hybrid, depending on project needsAbout OpalAIOpalAI is a deep-tech company developing Physical AI and intelligent systems for real-world and aerospace environments. Our work spans artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, computer vision, embedded computing, and advanced aerospace technologies.Our team brings experience from organizations including NASA/JPL, Caltech, USC, and UCLA, and we work on federally sponsored R&D programs aimed at translating advanced research into deployable technologies. This internship will support an OpalAI NASA SBIR project focused on improving the reliability and resilience of aerospace computing systems.Beyond traditional aircraft and spacecraft applications, the underlying technologies are also relevant to emerging computing architectures such as space-based data centers, orbital computing infrastructure, autonomous spacecraft, and distributed edge-computing systems, where reliable runtime monitoring, fault detection, and resilient operation are critical.Position OverviewWe are seeking a motivated Embedded Systems & FPGA Research Intern to contribute to a NASA-sponsored Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) project focused on runtime health monitoring and fault detection for safety-critical aerospace systems.The project explores hardware- and software-based techniques for monitoring the runtime behavior, integrity, and operational health of computing systems used in aircraft and spacecraft environments. The intern will work across technologies including embedded firmware, operating systems, runtime analysis, FPGA/RTL design, and system-level monitoring.These capabilities can support a broad range of next-generation aerospace computing platforms, including autonomous spacecraft, high-performance onboard computing, satellite constellations, and future space-based data centers, where systems may need to detect faults and maintain reliable operation with limited human intervention.This position is particularly well suited for a student or recent graduate interested in the intersection of embedded systems, computer architecture, FPGA design, cybersecurity and resilience, autonomous computing, and aerospace systems.ResponsibilitiesDepending on background and project needs, the intern may contribute to several of the following areas:Develop and evaluate techniques for runtime monitoring and analysis of embedded systems and firmware.Analyze firmware and operating-system behavior, including execution events, system calls, interrupts, memory activity, and other runtime characteristics.Design and implement hardware-based monitoring components on FPGA platforms.Develop, simulate, debug, and validate RTL designs using Verilog and/or SystemVerilog.Interface monitoring hardware with embedded processors and System-on-Chip (SoC) platforms.Develop software and firmware components for collecting, processing, and communicating runtime health and telemetry data.Integrate and evaluate sensors, data-acquisition components, and embedded communication interfaces.Design experiments and test environments to evaluate monitoring approaches under normal, degraded, and anomalous operating conditions.Collect and analyze experimental data and characterize system performance, resource utilization, latency, and monitoring coverage.Investigate architectures for resilient and autonomous computing in resource-constrained or remotely operated aerospace environments.Document designs, experiments, results, and technical findings in support of the NASA SBIR research effort.Contribute to prototype demonstrations and, where appropriate, technical reports, publications, and future research directions.Required QualificationsCandidates should be pursuing or have recently completed a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related discipline, with experience in several of the following areas:Embedded systems and embedded software development.C/C++ programming and low-level firmware development.Familiarity with firmware execution and runtime analysis.Understanding of operating-system concepts, including processes/threads, interrupts, memory management, scheduling, and device interaction.Digital logic and computer architecture fundamentals.Experience with Verilog and/or SystemVerilog.Familiarity with FPGA development, simulation, synthesis, or hardware debugging.Ability to work with integrated hardware/software systems and debug problems across multiple abstraction layers.Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.Preferred QualificationsExperience in any of the following areas is a plus:System-on-Chip (SoC) architectures and embedded processors.FPGA/SoC platforms such as AMD/Xilinx, Intel/Altera, or similar devices.ARM, RISC-V, or other embedded processor architectures.Embedded Linux, RTOS environments, bootloaders, or bare-metal firmware.Runtime tracing, performance monitoring, hardware performance counters, or firmware instrumentation.Sensor interfaces and data acquisition.Embedded communication protocols such as SPI, I²C, UART, CAN, Ethernet, or related aerospace/industrial interfaces.Hardware/software co-design.Fault detection, anomaly detection, runtime verification, or system health monitoring.Cybersecurity, trusted computing, or resilient computing architectures.Fault-tolerant, distributed, or autonomous computing systems.High-performance or edge computing in constrained environments.Safety-critical or high-reliability embedded systems.Aerospace, avionics, spacecraft, satellite, robotics, or autonomous-system applications.Interest in emerging areas such as orbital computing, space-based data centers, and autonomous space infrastructure.What You Will GainThis internship provides the opportunity to work on a multidisciplinary, NASA-sponsored R&D project connecting embedded computing, FPGA hardware, operating systems, runtime monitoring, and aerospace system reliability.The intern will gain hands-on experience developing and experimentally evaluating technologies intended for highly reliable and safety-critical computing environments. You will work closely with OpalAI's technical team and may contribute to:Prototype hardware and software development.FPGA and embedded-system experimentation.NASA SBIR technical demonstrations and reports.System architecture and research design.Experimental validation and performance analysis.Resilient and autonomous computing architectures for aerospace applications.Exploration of future applications including space-based data centers and distributed orbital computing infrastructure.Potential research publications and follow-on technology development.You will have the opportunity to work on problems where AI, embedded computing, hardware, and aerospace systems intersect, with an emphasis on translating research concepts into working prototypes.Who We Are Looking ForWe are looking for someone who enjoys understanding systems at a low level, is intellectually curious, and is comfortable moving between software, firmware, operating systems, and digital hardware.The ideal candidate enjoys building and debugging real systems, learning unfamiliar technologies quickly, and developing new approaches to improve the reliability, resilience, and intelligence of next-generation aerospace computing systems, including future autonomous spacecraft and space-based computing infrastructure.

jobs.description: Employer: The Wine Group Expires: 10/17/2026 Under the supervision of the Winemaker, Intern Winemaking duties will vary with the intent to participate in the overall wine quality from grape to finished product while following sustainable TWG practices. The intern will be required to spend a given amount of time shadowing different roles within the facility to gain knowledge and understand practices, processes while developing leadership skills.
